cls: Antitubercular - second-line bacteriostatic agent (aminosalicylic acid salt)
quick: 8-12 g/day in 2-3 divided doses (as PAS sodium)
Take with food or acidic drink to reduce GI upset
Use only if essential; part of MDR-TB regimens when needed
Avoid/adjust in significant renal impairment (sodium and metabolite load)
Caution; can cause hepatitis - monitor LFTs
summary: Sodium aminosalicylate (sodium PAS) is a bacteriostatic second-line antitubercular agent used as part of combination therapy for drug-resistant (multidrug-resistant) tuberculosis. It inhibits folate synthesis in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It is never used alone, is associated with frequent gastrointestinal intolerance, hypothyroidism (especially with ethionamide), and hepatitis, and carries a notable sodium load. It is a WHO essential medicine; the sodium salt is largely used outside the US FDA-approved granule formulation.
indications: Treatment of multidrug-resistant pulmonary and extrapulmonary tuberculosis as part of combination regimens
Treatment of tuberculosis caused by organisms resistant to or intolerant of first-line agents (never as monotherapy)

dosage.n: Always with other anti-TB drugs; titrate to limit GI intolerance
Maximum about 10-12 g/day; weight-band dosing per WHO

admin: Always use combined with other effective anti-TB agents - never alone
Take with food or an acidic beverage (e.g., orange/tomato juice or yogurt) to reduce GI upset
Swallow granule formulations whole; do not crush or chew enteric/granule products
Maintain adequate hydration; complete the full prolonged course
moa: Aminosalicylic acid is a structural analogue of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA). It competitively inhibits dihydropteroate synthase in the mycobacterial folate pathway, blocking folic acid synthesis and producing a bacteriostatic effect against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It also impairs mycobactin synthesis and iron uptake.

absolute: Severe renal impairment / end-stage renal disease (metabolite and sodium accumulation)
relative: Congestive heart failure or sodium-restricted states (high sodium content)

preg: Use only if essential and no safer alternative exists, as part of a multidrug regimen for resistant TB. Untreated TB is itself hazardous in pregnancy; weigh benefit against potential risk.
lact: Small amounts pass into breast milk. Use with caution; monitor the infant. Many guidelines permit breastfeeding with appropriate maternal TB treatment.
renal: Aminosalicylate metabolites and the sodium salt accumulate in renal impairment. Avoid or markedly reduce dose in significant renal dysfunction; contraindicated in severe impairment/ESRD.
hepatic: Can cause hepatitis. Use with caution in hepatic impairment, monitor LFTs, and discontinue if significant transaminase elevation or jaundice develops.

major: Ethionamide (markedly increased risk of hypothyroidism and hepatotoxicity)
moderate: Vitamin B12 (impaired absorption with prolonged use)
minor: Rifampicin (PAS granule excipients may reduce rifampicin absorption if taken together)
interactions.food: Take with food/acidic drink; food reduces GI upset
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine glucose tests and alter thyroid function tests

serious: Hypersensitivity reactions with fever and rash
rare: Encephalopathy, vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use

monitoring: Liver function tests at baseline and periodically
Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), especially when combined with ethionamide
Serum sodium and electrolytes (high sodium content)
counsel: Take with meals or a sour drink to ease stomach upset
Never take this drug by itself - it is one part of your TB treatment
Complete the full course even if you feel better - stopping early breeds resistance
Report yellowing of eyes/skin, severe stomach upset, fatigue, or neck swelling
pk: Bacteriostatic action over days within a combination regimen
Plasma peak around 1-2 hours after an oral dose
Approximately 1 hour (short); rapidly acetylated and renally excreted
Short half-life requires divided daily dosing
Store in a cool, dry place below 15-25 C, protected from light and moisture; discoloured/brown product should be discarded
pearls: Bacteriostatic PABA analogue - blocks folate synthesis in M. tuberculosis; always used in combination, never alone
Strongly goitrogenic, especially with ethionamide - monitor thyroid function and consider levothyroxine if hypothyroidism develops
High sodium content matters in heart failure, hypertension, and renal impairment
WHO essential medicine for MDR-TB; the sodium salt is used largely outside the US FDA-approved delayed-release granule (note regional sourcing)
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up. Consistent dosing is critical to prevent TB drug resistance.
overdose: Overdose may cause severe gastrointestinal effects, crystalluria, metabolic acidosis, and salicylate-like toxicity. Management is supportive: hydration, correction of electrolyte/acid-base disturbances, and urine alkalinization; consider gastric decontamination if recent and large.
refs: WHO Operational Handbook on Tuberculosis - Drug-resistant TB treatment
